items.text: European Union leaders agreed to initiate accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova, granting formal candidate status to Georgia. Ukraine, a candidate since 2022, has a history of EU relations dating back 30 years, marked by the Orange Revolution and the 2014 Maidan Revolution. Moldova, a candidate since 2022, had to address issues like judiciary reform and anti-corruption measures to start accession talks. Turkey, a candidate since 1999, faces a freeze on accession talks due to human rights concerns. Other Western Balkan nations, like North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, have different stages of negotiations. EU leaders also recognized Kosovo’s EU perspective in 2022, although not all member states recognize its independence. Difficult words: accession (the act of formally joining a group), judiciary (the system of courts in a country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

EU leaders recently agreed to begin accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova, and they granted Georgia formal candidate status. Ukraine became a candidate in 2022. The country has a history of 30 years of EU relations. Moldova also became a candidate in 2022, but the country has change how courts work and solve corruption before accession talks can start. Turkey became a candidate in 1999, but the EU has concerns about human rights in the country. Therefore, there are no talks at the moment. Other countries like North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, have different stages of negotiations. The EU also recognized Kosovo’s EU perspective in 2022, but not all member states see Kosovo as an independent country. Difficult words: accession (formally joining a group), grant (to agree to give or allow), perspective (outlook). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European leaders start talking about Ukraine and Moldova joining the European Union. They also say that Georgia has a chance too. Ukraine wants to be an EU member since 2022. The country has a long history with the EU, almost 30 years. Moldova also wants to join the EU. Also from 2022. But first, the country has to change its courts and stop corruption . Then, they can start talking about joining the EU. Turkey wants to join since 1999. But the EU stops talking about it. Turkey has problems with human rights . More countries countries want to join. They are North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. They are at different points in joining. EU leaders also say that Kosovo may join. Not all countries agree. Some countries say that Kosovo is not an independent country. Difficult words: join (to become part of a group), corruption (when important people, like politicians, do bad things), human rights (things which every person can do or have). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Royal Mint has collaborated with the Natural History Museum to release a new set of dinosaur-themed collectable coins. The three-coin collection features the tyrannosaurus, stegosaurus, and diplodocus, each appearing on their own coin. Designed by artist Robert Nicholls with guidance from the Natural History Museum, some coins depict dinosaurs in their habitat using color. Prices start from £11. Rebecca Morgan, director of commemorative coin at the Royal Mint, expressed excitement about the new collectables, while Maxine Lister, head of licensing at the Natural History Museum, highlighted the iconic dinosaurs immortalized on the 50p coins. The collection, part of the Mint’s Tales of the Earth series, is available for purchase on the Royal Mint’s website. Difficult words: collectable (desirable and valued by collectors), commemorative (acting as a memorial of an event or person), immortalized (remembered for a very long time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Royal Mint together with the Natural History Museum launched a new set of coins which feature dinosaurs. The three-coin collection showcases the tyrannosaurus, stegosaurus, and diplodocus, each on its own coin. Artist Robert Nicholls designed the coins with the help by the museum. Some of the coins include color to depict dinosaurs in their habitat . Prices start at £11. This release is part of the Mint’s Tales of the Earth series, which celebrate ancient creatures and dinosaurs. If you like dinosaurs, you can buy the coins on the Royal Mint’s website. Difficult words: showcase (to show), habitat (the place where an animal or plant naturally lives), depict (to represent by drawing or painting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Royal Mint and the Natural History Museum make special coins with dinosaurs. There are three coins with different dinosaurs – tyrannosaurus, stegosaurus, and diplodocus. The coins have pictures by artist Robert Nicholls. Some are colorful. They show dinosaurs in places where they naturally live. Rebecca Morgan from the Royal Mint is happy about these new coins. Maxine Lister from the Natural History Museum likes that the coins have famous dinosaurs. These coins are part of a series which celebrates old animals and dinosaurs. You can get them from the Royal Mint’s website. The price starts at £11. Difficult words: coin (small round piece of metal which people use ad money), series (a number of similar events or objects which come one after another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Google’s 2023 Year in Search revealed that the Israel-Hamas war dominated global queries , with terms like ‘War in Israel and Gaza’, ‘what is Hamas’, and ‘why did Hamas attack’ topping search lists. Following the war, the Titan submersible’s implosion during a Titanic wreckage expedition and the Turkey-Syria earthquake were notable global news trends. The roundup also highlighted events and individuals, including Damar Hamlin’s NFL game cardiac arrest, actor Matthew Perry’s death, and trending personalities like Jeremy Renner and Andrew Tate. The list featured movies such as ‘Barbie’ and ‘Oppenheimer’, TV shows like ‘The Last of Us’ and ‘Ginny and Georgia’, and songs like Yoasobi’s ‘Idol’ and Jason Aldean’s ‘Try That in a Small Town’. Language trends included the Oxford word of the year, ‘Rizz’, representing charisma. Difficult words: query (a question), roundup (a summary), trending (currently popular or widely discussed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

If you searched on Google in recent months to understand the Israel-Hamas war, you are not alone. Google’s 2023 Year in Search showed that people worldwide were looking for information about Hamas. ‘War in Israel and Gaza’ was the top news trend in the US and globally. Other searches included ‘what is Hamas’, ‘what is happening in Israel’, and ‘why did Hamas attack’. The Titan submersible’s implosion and the Turkey-Syria earthquake were also important global news trends. Other top searches included major events and individuals, for example, Damar Hamlin’s NFL game health problems, actor Matthew Perry’s death, and trending personalities like Jeremy Renner and Andrew Tate. There were also movies ‘Barbie’ and ‘Oppenheimer’ on the list. Difficult words: submersible (a small boat which people use for research), major (big or important), trending (popular at the moment). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Every year, Google makes a list of top searches. It tells us what information people search on the internet the most. In 2023, people around the world want to know about Hamas. They search for things like ‘war in Israel and Gaza’, ‘what is Hamas’, or ‘what is happening in Israel’. Other top searches include incidents such as the Titan submersible accident and the Turkey-Syria. The list includes the most important events and people, like Damar Hamlin’s NFL game injury , actor Matthew Perry’s death, and popular figures like Jeremy Renner and Andrew Tate. With movies, ‘Barbie’ and ‘Oppenheimer’ are among the most popular searches. Difficult words: submersible (a small boat which scientists often use), injury (when you get hurt), figure (a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In a shocking incident, two intruders entered the lower house of India’s parliament, shouting slogans and releasing yellow smoke. Lawmakers and security quickly apprehended them. The intruders were reportedly shouting ‘tanashahi Nehi Chaliga’, meaning ‘dictatorship will not last’. Two more accomplices were arrested outside, with one claiming to be a protesting student concerned about unemployment. The incident occurred while lawmakers were in session in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the parliament. Both houses were suspended for a short period before the session resumed. This incident occurred on the 22nd anniversary of a 2001 deadly militant attack on the Indian parliament, where gunmen killed nine security officers, leading to heightened tensions between India and Pakistan. Difficult words: apprehend (to catch or arrest), accomplice (a person who helps another commit a crime). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A surprising incident happened in India’s parliament. Two men entered the building, released yellow smoke, and shouted. Both houses of parliament stopped working for some time but police and security quickly caught the men and took them to custody. They also arrested two more people outside the building. Reportedly, one of the men was a student who protested against unemployment . This incident happened on the 22nd anniversary of a 2001 terror attack on the Indian parliament, where gunmen killed nine security officers. The attack brought more tensions between India and Pakistan. Difficult words: unemployment (when many people are without a job), tension (a situation when people or groups are nervous and they don’t trust each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An unpleasant incident happens in India’s parliament. Two people go inside. They released yellow smoke. They shout. Police and security quickly catch the men. They also arrest two more people outside the building. One man is a student. He protests against unemployment . Both houses of the parliament stop work. The incident scares many people. It happens on the 22nd anniversary of a 2001 attack on the parliament. Gunmen kill nine officers. India blames another group from Pakistan. The incident causes more problems with Pakistan. Difficult words: release (to let something go or flow), unemployment (when people do not have a job), anniversary (the day on which something important happens in the past). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After two weeks of at times fractious negotiations in the United Arab Emirates, the COP28 climate summit concluded with a groundbreaking deal urging all nations to transition away from fossil fuels to combat climate change. Despite criticism for lacking a clear commitment to phase out fossil fuels, the agreement calls for a just and equitable global shift from fossil fuels to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. Cop28 president Sultan Al Jaber emphasized its historic nature and a comprehensive response to the global stocktake that revealed inadequate adherence to the Paris Climate Agreement. While praised for advocating a move away from coal, oil, and gas, critics cited failures in emission reductions, finance for vulnerable nations, and unclear language favoring fossil fuel interests. Difficult words: phase out (to gradually stop using something), equitable (fair and impartial), adherence (obeying a rule or law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The COP28 summit which took place in the United Arab Emirates concluded with a significant deal. The deal asks nations to shift away from fossil fuels to deal with climate change. Some people criticize the deal because there is not a clear commitment to stop using fossil fuels, but the deal calls for a global transition towards net-zero emissions by 2050. Cop28 president Sultan Al Jaber emphasized its historic nature because countries didn’t follow the Paris Agreement. Many people see the deal as a move away from coal, oil, and gas, but others argue that it doesn’t do enough to reduce pollution and help countries which are the most affected by climate change. The next meeting, COP29, will be in Baku, Azerbaijan, next November. Difficult words: significant (very important), commitment (a promise or decision to do something), transition (change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Cop28 summit takes place in the United Arab Emirates. It lasts two weeks. Nearly 200 countries speak about climate change. COP28 ends with a deal. Countries must stop using fossil fuels . It is the only way to stop climate change. The deal says that all nations should reach zero emissions by 2050. The summit president, Sultan Al Jaber, says that it is a big and historic response to the Paris Agreement. Countries do not follow the Paris agreement. Some people are happy with the deal. But others say that it does not do enough to stop pollution. Some countries need more help because of changing weather. The next meeting, COP29, will be in Baku, Azerbaijan, next November. Difficult words: fossil fuels (coal, oil, and gas), historic (very important), pollution (making the air, water or soil dirty). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There was shocking footage filmed in front of an English hospital’s A&E department. It showed a man collapsing to the ground in the pain of a heart attack and being unattended for a whole 30 seconds, after which a standing-by paramedic went to see him without taking any medical equipment. The paramedic talked to the man for about two minutes and then returned to his ambulance. The man on the ground died. The courts handed this paramedic an eight-month sentence, suspended him for two years and ordered him to complete 240 hours of community service . Difficult words: A&E (Accident and Emergency), suspend (to make somebody stop working), community service (unpaid work which normal people can do and criminals must do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man was having a heart attack in front of a hospital in England. He fell to the ground in pain. A paramedic sat in a nearby ambulance and saw what was happening. However, he did not attend to the dying man or 30 seconds. Then the paramedic left his ambulance and went to him. He didn’t take any medical equipment with him – he just talked to him for around two minutes. He then returned to his ambulance. The paramedic let the man die. Authorities ordered 240 hours of community service and the paramedic no longer works in that job. Difficult words: paramedic (somebody who does medical work but is not a doctor), attend (to help), community service (unpaid work which normal people can do and criminals must do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man is in front of a hospital. He is having a heart attack . He is in pain. He falls to the ground. An ambulance is parked nearby. A paramedic sits in the ambulance. He just watches the man. After 30 seconds, the paramedic goes to him. He does not help him. The two men only talk. The paramedic then returns to the ambulance. The man on the ground dies. The paramedic loses his job. He must do 240 hours of community service, too. Difficult words: heart attack (a serious condition when somebody’s heart stops working normally), paramedic (somebody who does medical work but is not a doctor), community service (unpaid work which normal people can do and criminals must do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe has achieved a preliminary agreement on groundbreaking European Union regulations for artificial intelligence (AI), covering government use of AI in biometric surveillance and regulating AI systems like ChatGPT. This political breakthrough positions the EU as a leading global standard-setter in AI legislation, marking a historic day according to European Commissioner Thierry Breton. The agreement mandates transparency obligations for foundation models, such as ChatGPT, and general-purpose AI systems (GPAI) before entering the market. These include technical documentation, compliance with EU copyright law, and detailed summaries about training content. High-impact foundation models face additional requirements, including model evaluations, risk assessments, adversarial testing , reporting incidents to the European Commission, cybersecurity assurance, and energy efficiency reports. Governments are restricted in using real-time biometric surveillance, permitted only in specific crime cases or imminent threats, such as terrorist attacks. Difficult words: standard-setter (an organization or group that establishes and maintains standards for a particular field or industry), mandate (to require something to be done), adversarial testing (examining systems by attempting to exploit weaknesses). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Europe is ready to make a deal which will regulate artificial intelligence (AI). The deal will tell governments how to use AI in biometric surveillance and AI systems like ChatGPT. It is an important moment for Europe which establishes rules about AI in the world. According to the deal, models such as ChatGPT, and general-purpose AI systems (GPAI) will have to be transparent before they enter the market. There must be technical documentation which will follow EU copyright law. Besides this, new AI models will have to go through many tests and governments must report all incidents to the European Commission. Governments will have only limited possibility to use real-time biometric surveillance, allowed only in specific crime cases or terrorist attacks. Difficult words: regulate (to control by rules), biometric surveillance (video cameras which capture people’s faces or eyes), transparent (clear). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe makes stricter rules for artificial intelligence (AI). The rules say how governments can use AI. These rules are about systems which watch people and systems like ChatGPT. Europe will be the first to make these laws. Leaders talk for a long time to agree on the rules. Computers to be clear before people and organizations can buy them. They will share how they work and what they learn. European Commission must know about all incidents and dangerous situations. There are special video cameras. They watch people. They can scan their eyes. The new rule says that AI can watch only criminals or terrorists . It is not possible to watch people in the streets. Difficult words: criminal (a person who breaks rules), terrorist (a person who hurts many other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Your lost belongings, including that favorite shirt left behind during a flight to California, might be on sale at the Unclaimed Baggage store in Scottsboro, Alabama. Operating for over 50 years, this 4,600-square-meter store houses items left unclaimed for at least nine days by airlines. The store, a shopping destination rather than a typical lost and found, attracts visitors like Susan Boatman, who travels from afar to discover treasures. Founded in 1970 by entrepreneur Doyle Owens, the store started when Owens bought unclaimed baggage in Washington DC for 300 dollars and sold out on the first day. While 99.5% of bags are usually reunited with their owners, the remaining items are sold or recycled, with some even ending up in a museum at the store. Difficult words: entrepreneur (a person who sets up a business), unclaimed (not collected or retrieved). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Do you sometimes wonder where your lost belongings end up? They could be for sale at the Unclaimed Baggage store in Alabama, California. The store started operating over 50 years ago. This huge 4,600-square-meter store sells items left unclaimed by airlines for at least nine days. This is not a usual lost and found store, people come here to buy things which nobody wants. Doyle Owens founded the store in 1970, when he sold unclaimed baggage which he bought in Washington DC. While 99.5% of bags usually find their owners. Owens sells or recycles the rest, or even puts it in a store museum. Difficult words: belongings (things which belong to you), unclaimed (things which nobody wants back). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Do you ever lose something on a trip? Maybe your favorite shirt is at a big store in Alabama, California. This store sells things which people forget on planes. Airlines keep these things for nine days. If nobody asks for them, people can buy them. Some shops buy these things. Doyle Owens starts his store in 1970. He buys unclaimed baggage . He sells everything on the first day. The store usually sells only a third of what it gets. He recycles some things, too. Some things even go to a museum in the store. Difficult words: unclaimed (things which nobody wants back), baggage (bags and suitcases), recycle (to use again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police Constable Hutton and hit team from England were involved in a high-speed chase when they used stinger devices to bring the car to a stop. The four young people in the vehicle started to run away, but quick thinking and one unusual tactic stopped one man from getting away. The PC was able to bark so realistically that everyone around thought that he had a trained canine with him . The policeman has been the subject of a fair few jokes since the incident, but who cares if people think that you are barking mad if it means that you get your man ? Difficult words: hit team (specially trained police), chase (driving after somebody to try to catch him or her), stinger devices (tools with a lot of big sharp needles), PC (police constable), canine (a dog), fair (a lot of something), barking mad (very crazy), get your man (catch the bad guy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A police officer in England caught a man by pretending to be a dog. The policeman was chasing a man and barked at him so realistically that everyone around thought that he had a trained dog with him. It all started on the streets of southwest England on Thursday. The policeman and his team were involved in a high speed chase. They stopped the car with four young people inside but they tried to run away. When the people were running away, the policeman started to bark like a dog, and one young man stopped. Since the incident, other people made some jokes about the policeman, but he does not care. His tactic worked and it is all that matters. Difficult words: chase (run after), be involved in (be part of). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from England. Policemen want to stop a car. They are successful. There are four young people in the car. The car stops. The four young people try to run away. The policemen want to stop them. The young people are fast. One policeman has an idea. He starts to bark like a dog. He is very realistic . People think that he is a real dog. One young man stops and he does not run away. People make jokes about the policeman because he barks like a dog. This is not important to him. His tactic is good and it is important. Difficult words: bark (make sounds like a dog), realistic (like real life). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Protesters under the banner Workers for a Free Palestine successfully closed four UK arms factories producing components for Israeli F-35 fighter jets. The factories include Eaton Mission Systems, BAE Systems at Samlesbury Aerodrome, L3Harris in Brighton, and BAE Govan in Glasgow. These factories supply parts for F-35 stealth combat aircraft used by Israel in Gaza. The diverse group of protesters, including health workers, teachers, and artists, is demanding an end to arms sales to Israel and a permanent UK-backed ceasefire . The coordinated blockades align with similar actions in France, Denmark, and the Netherlands. Difficult words: ceasefire (an agreement to temporarily stop fighting), blockade (surrounding or closing a place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Protesters shut down four UK arms factories which produce components for Israeli F-35 fighter jets. The factories are located in Bournemouth, Lancashire, Brighton, and Glasgow, and they supply important parts for the F-35 stealth fighter. Currently, Israel is using these jets in Gaza. The diverse group of protesters included health workers and teachers. They demand stopping arms sales to Israel and securing a lasting ceasefire with UK government support. Similar actions are taking place in France, Denmark, and the Netherlands. They reflect an escalating movement against Israeli arms manufacturing in Europe. Difficult words: component (a part of a machine or vehicle), ceasefire (the time when two countries stop fighting), escalate (to become greater or more serious). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Factories in Europe make parts for Israel’s fighter planes. Israel uses these planes to attack Gaza. Protesters in the UK stop four factories. The factories are in Bournemouth, Lancashire, Brighton, and Glasgow. The protesters want the UK to stop selling weapons to Israel. They want peace . Workers from different jobs, like health workers and teachers, join the protest. People ask the government to stop support for Israel. Similar things happen in factories in France, Denmark, and the Netherlands. More and more people want the war to stop. People in Europe do not want to make weapons for Israel. Difficult words: peace (the time when nobody fights), join (to become a part of something), support (help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dog lovers in Lagos celebrated the annual Lagos Dog Carnival, challenging stereotypes about pet ownership in Nigeria, where dogs are sometimes bred for meat. Organized by Jackie Idimogu, the festival aims to change perceptions and highlight the love and care dogs deserve. The event showcased various breeds, including American Eskimos, French Bulldogs, and Golden Retrievers, dressed in colorful outfits, contributing to the theme ‘Splash of Colors’. Pasha, a six-year-old Caucasian Shepherd mix, won the Dog of the Year title. Idimogu emphasized the educational aspect of the festival, informing attendees about proper pet care and understanding their needs. The event fosters a sense of community among dog owners and promotes responsible pet ownership. Difficult words: stereotype (a widely held idea of a particular type of person or thing), perception (the way something is understood or interpreted), foster (to encourage the development of). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Dog lovers in Lagos celebrated the annual Lagos Dog Carnival. Something like that is not easy in a country where some people still eat dog meat. Jackie Idimogu organized the festival and his main idea was to change people’s view on dogs and point out that dogs need love and care. There were various breeds , such as American Eskimos and French Bulldogs, dressed in colorful outfits . Pasha, a six-year-old Caucasian Shepherd mix, won the title of Dog of the Year. Idimogu said that he wanted to inform people about good pet care. The event was a good opportunity for dog lovers to meet and share their tips on how to look after dogs well. Difficult words: breed (a type of animal or plant), outfit (clothes which you wear together), opportunity (a situation when it is good to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dog Festival is in Lagos, Nigeria. People who love dogs can meet. But it is not easy to plan such a festival. Many people in Nigeria eat dogs. The festival shows that dogs are not only for guarding or eating. The festival takes place every year. Different kinds of dogs wear pretty clothes in many colors. A dog called Pasha becomes the Dog of the Year. The festival teaches people how to look after dogs. It also makes Nigerians love dogs more. Dog owners meet and have fun together. Difficult words: guard (to watch a place and keep it safe), owner (a person who has something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to The Economist Intelligence Unit’s Cost of Living Index , Singapore and Zurich have surpassed New York as the world’s most expensive cities. The index considers prices of various products and services, including transport, rent, food, and alcohol, in 173 cities globally. Geneva, New York, and Hong Kong complete the top five. Global prices rose by 7.4% year-on-year, a slight decrease from the previous year’s 8.8% increase. Grocery prices continued to rise due to manufacturers and retailers passing on costs to consumers. Increased demand for post-pandemic travel led to a significant climb in transport prices. The EIU anticipates interest rate rises, economic activity slowdown, and dampened consumer demand in 2024. Potential factors affecting costs include the Israel-Hamas conflict and El Niño impacting food prices. Difficult words: index (a sign or measure of something), anticipate (to expect or predict), dampen (to make less strong or intense). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Singapore and Zurich are now more expensive than New York, according to the EIU Index. The index analyzes prices for things goods and services in 173 world cities globally, for example, transport, rent, food, and alcohol. Geneva, New York, and Hong Kong are among the top five most expensive cities. Global prices increased by 7.4%, which was a little less than in the previous year. Food prices continued to rise, while strong demand for traveling after the pandemic meant an increase in transport prices. In 2024, experts expect higher interest rates , less business activity, and consumer demand. Difficult words: index (a sign or measure of something), demand (when many people want to buy something), interest rate (extra money which you pay for borrowing money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New York is no longer the most expensive city to live in. Singapore and Zurich are now the top two. This is according to the EIU index . It looks at prices for things like transportation , rent , food, and alcohol in 173 cities worldwide. Geneva, New York, and Hong Kong are also very expensive places to live. The global prices go up by 7.4% when we compare them to the previous year. Food prices are also rising. Travel prices are going up because more people want to travel after the pandemic. For 2024, the EIU thinks that prices will go up, businesses will slow down, and people will buy less. Difficult words: index (a number or symbol which helps us measure something), transportation (moving things or people from one place to another), rent (money which someone must pay every month for using a house or flat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US House Republicans questioned university presidents, including Claudine Gay of Harvard, Liz Magill of the University of Pennsylvania, and Sally Kornbluth of MIT, about their efforts to combat antisemitism following a Hamas attack on Israel. While denouncing the attack and expressing commitment to ensuring Jewish students’ safety, the presidents faced criticism for what some deemed inadequate responses to antisemitic incidents on campus. The issue revolves around clashes between pro-Palestinian and pro-Israel demonstrations, leading to concerns about antisemitic and Islamophobic rhetoric . Harvard and Penn, in particular, have faced backlash over their responses to alleged antisemitic behavior, such as a Palestinian Writers festival. House Republicans pressed the presidents on these incidents, questioning their actions and responses. Difficult words: denounce (to publicly declare as wrong or evil), rhetoric (language designed to have a persuasive or impressive effect), backlash (a strong negative reaction by a large number of people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US House Republicans questioned presidents of three universities regarding their efforts to deal with antisemitism after a Hamas attack on Israel on October 7. During their testimony , the presidents criticized the attack. They confirmed that Jewish students’ safety was very important, but at the same time, they protected free speech on campuses . The universities faced criticism, especially Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania. Some people said that the universities reacted slowly to antisemitic incidents after pro-Palestinian and pro-Israel demonstrations. House Republicans pressed the presidents on several incidents and they expressed worries about campus safety. Difficult words: antisemitism (bad feelings towards Jewish people), testimony (a formal statement), campus (the grounds and buildings of a university or college). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some US politicians ask university presidents about antisemitic incidents. These are three universities. Problems start after Hamas attacks Israel on October 7. The presidents strongly disagree with the attack. They say that Jewish students are safe. But they also say that free speech is important. Some universities, especially Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, do not react fast enough to antisemitic incidents. At least some people say that. Officials ask for better safety at universities and at specific events which could bring problems, such as pro-Palestinian and pro-Israel protests. Difficult words: antisemitic (against Jewish people), free speech (when anyone can say what they want), safety (a safe place or situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greek olive growers, who are facing a challenging harvest, are confronting a rise in thefts as prices increase. Panagiotis Tsafaras, a seasoned grower, has experienced thefts twice, losing over a ton of olives in one incident. Such thefts are unprecedented in the region, prompting growers to take measures like installing cameras, and GPS trackers, and even considering private security. Thieves operate mainly at night, and they employ various tactics , such as using rods to knock olives off trees or silent electric chainsaws to cut entire branches. This surge in olive theft is a nationwide issue, confirmed by Greek police. Greece, the world’s third-largest olive oil producer, is known for its high-quality extra virgin variety. This year’s production is anticipated to drop by up to 50% due to adverse weather conditions. Difficult words: confront (to deal with a problem or difficulty), unprecedented (never done or known before), tactic (a planned way of doing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Greek olive growers are having problems. This year’s harvest is poor, and as prices are growing, there are more thefts . Panagiotis Tsafaras, a grower from Filiatra, walks round his groves twice a day to protect them against thieves. Thieves stole over a ton of olives in a single incident. Nothing like that ever happened before in the region, and growers have to take measures to stop the thieves. They install cameras and GPS trackers. Thieves come mainly at night, and they use rods or silent electric chainsaws to steal olives. Greek police confirm a big increase in olive thefts across the country. Greece is the world’s third-largest olive oil producer. Due to bad weather, this year, growers produced 50% less than the year before. Difficult words: theft (an incident when a person steals something), measure (an action which someone takes to achieve something), chainsaw (an instrument for cutting trees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greek olive growers have a hard time. The weather is bad this year. This year’s harvest may be 50% less than last year’s. Prices of olives and olive oil are going up. Thieves are stealing more because of this. Panagiotis Tsafaras grows olives. He checks his groves twice every day. He wants to stop thieves. In one incident, thieves steal over a ton of olives. This problem is new to the area. Growers start using cameras and GPS to watch their olives. Thieves come at night. They are very quiet. Greek police say that such incidents are all over the country. Greece is the third-biggest olive oil maker in the year. Difficult words: harvest (the time of the year when farmers pick grain, fruit, and vegetables), thief (the person who steals something), grove (a small wood or other group of trees). China’s recent visa-free travel policy, implemented on December 1, has positively impacted tourism. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs aims to continually adjust visa policies to enhance cross-border travel conditions. Approximately 7,000 out of nearly 18,000 travelers from France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and Malaysia entered China in the initial three days of December. Daily average tourist numbers from these countries increased by 39% in the first three days compared to the last day of November. This move is part of China’s efforts to revive its tourism sector post-COVID-19 restrictions. The government also seeks to improve its global image, as revealed by a recent survey that indicated negative perceptions of China in 24 countries. Difficult words: enhance (to intensify or improve), revive (to give new strength or energy to). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

China’s new visa-free travel policy came into effect on December 1. So far, it seems that it positively impacted tourism. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs plans to adjust visa policies to make traveling to and from China even easier. In the first three days of December, about 7,000 travelers from France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and Malaysia entered China. Daily average tourist numbers from these countries increased by 39%, compared to the last day of November. China wants to give new energy to its tourism sector after COVID-19. A recent survey found that 24 countries had negative ideas about China, so another reason for the visa-free policy is to improve China’s reputation in the world. Difficult words: adjust (to change), average (a standard or level that is typical or usual), reputation (what people generally think about someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: visa (an official document which says that you can enter a country), necessary (something what you need to do), improve (to make something better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Venezuelans participated in a referendum supported by President Nicolas Maduro, addressing a border dispute with Guyana. The dispute involves a question about rejecting the jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) over territory around the Essequibo River, a potentially oil-rich land. The referendum aims to gauge support for Maduro’s government ahead of the 2024 presidential election. Despite Guyana’s request to halt the referendum, the ICJ ruled without forbidding it and urged both parties to avoid actions that worsen the dispute. Maduro cast his vote and encouraged approval. Political analysts believe Maduro is using the referendum to test electoral strength, expecting it to pass due to a lack of opposition campaigning. Voters expressed hopes of reclaiming the disputed territory. Difficult words: jurisdiction (legal authority or control), gauge (to assess or measure), electoral (relating to elections). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last weekend, Venezuelans voted in a referendum backed by President Nicolas Maduro. The referendum was about a problem with Guyana. The Essequibo River territory is in Guyana, near the border with Venezuela, and Venezuela wants it back. Some people believe that the area is rich in oil. Guyana requested to stop the referendum, but the International Court of Justice didn’t forbid it and asked both countries not to make the situation even worse. Experts believe that Maduro is using the referendum to test his strength before the 2024 presidential elections, and they expect it to pass because there is no strong opposition . Voters hope to get the territory back. Difficult words: referendum (when people vote about a specific case), request (to ask someone to do something), opposition (a group of people in a government who have different ideas from the main party). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people believe that there is oil in the ground. Venezuela wants this area. The International Court of Justice does not say no to the referendum. But the court asks both countries not to make the problem even worse. Maduro wants to see if people like his government. People will choose a new president in 2024. Difficult words: referendum (when people vote about a specific problem), territory (a piece of land), border (the line between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People estimate that more than 1.5 million children in Indonesia work in the agricultural sector – mainly in tobacco, rubber, and palm oil plantations. Those who work on tobacco farms plant it, apply pesticides , harvest , bundle and dry the leaves, and do all of this mostly with bare hands. The working conditions are hazardous and the children suffer from ‘green tobacco sickness’ – acute nicotine poisoning. Some of the symptoms they commonly experience are nausea , headaches, and dizzy spells . In Indonesia, hiring children under 15 years of age is illegal, but traders or companies do not directly hire children. They skip school or drop out altogether in order to help their families make a living. One day’s work earns them an equivalent of a dollar a day. The firms who buy the tobacco never question the process behind the production, which is what groups like Human Rights Watch are trying to change. They reached out to some of the biggest companies operating in Indonesia, asking them to educate the families about the dangers of this work. Indonesia is one of a few countries that have not signed the World Health Organization’s Framework Convention on Tobacco Control – a global public health treaty aimed at protecting the population from the consequences of tobacco consumption and exposure to tobacco smoke. Difficult words: pesticide (something which kills insects), harvest (gather, get), bundle (tie or roll up together), hazardous (dangerous), nausea (a feeling of sickness), dizzy (weak, not feeling well), spell (a short period of time), treaty (an agreement, a deal, a pact). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Indonesia is the 5th biggest producer of tobacco. Hiring children under 15 years of age in Indonesia is illegal but around 1.5 million children work in Indonesia’s agriculture . Thousands of them work on rubber, palm oil, and tobacco plantations . Many of them suffer from “green tobacco sickness” – they get headaches, get dizzy and sick. They skip school to help their families make money, but they make only one dollar a day. Human rights groups are trying to change things. They ask the biggest companies in Indonesia to educate the families about the dangers. Difficult words: agriculture (farming), plantation (a large farm that grows a plant that makes a lot of money like coffee or tobacco), dizzy (weak, not feeling well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

While on safari in South Africa, Arnold Schwarzenegger, the American actor known for playing the Terminator, had a very close encounter with an elephant. Someone filmed a video of the elephant getting a little too close to the car, which he shared with his 5.4 million followers on Instagram just after it happened. The dramatic meeting, however, did not put him off elephants. He tweeted that he is in awe of them and wishes people would stop killing them for their ivory and to take a photo instead of a shot . Difficult words: encounter (a meeting), be in awe of (feel awe for – a feeling of respect mixed with fear or wonder), ivory (the material of an elephant’s tusks – the two big horns that come out of the front of the elephant), shot (a shot from a gun). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Terminator met an elephant. While on safari in South Africa, Arnold Schwarzenegger had a very close encounter with an elephant. He shared the video with his 5.4 million followers on Instagram just after it happened. An elephant was moving around his car. When the car started to move, it started running behind it. The experience did not put Schwarzenegger off . He tweeted that people should stop killing elephants, and that they should take a photo, not a shot . Difficult words: encounter (a meeting), experience (something which happens to you), put off (when something makes you feel uncomfortable), shot (this is a pun as it means two things – a shot from a gun and a photo can be called a shot). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The elephant starts to run behind the car. This is a little scary. Schwarzenegger films this. He shares the video with his 5.4 million followers on Instagram. He says that people should not kill elephants. Difficult words: share (to show or give something to other people), follower (when a person watches somebody on Instagram, Twitter, or Facebook), should not (it is good not to do it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In an eight-week-long operation since October 27, Israeli forces discovered 800 shafts leading to Hamas’ extensive network of tunnels in Gaza. Over half of these shafts have been destroyed. Hamas claimed to have a tunnel system comparable in size to the New York subway, serving as both protection and operational bases. Israeli strikes targeted these tunnels situated in civilian areas, often near or inside buildings like schools and mosques. The military employed penetrating munitions, mapping robots, and explosive gel to neutralize the passages. Concerns about civilian casualties have prompted international worry, with the United States urging Israel to exercise caution. Of the 800 shafts found, 500 have been destroyed using various methods, including detonation and sealing off, along with damage to many miles of main tunnel routes. Difficult words: penetrating (to get access to a place or system, especially when this is difficult to do), neutralize (to make something no longer effective or dangerous), detonation (making something explode). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On October 27, Israeli forces started a ground operation and they discovered a network of tunnels in Gaza. There were about 800 shafts and Israeli soldiers already destroyed more than half of them. Hamas said that their tunnel system was as big as the New York subway. They use it for both protection and operational purposes . Israeli bombs hit these tunnels in civilian areas, often near buildings like schools and mosques. The military used different ways to destroy the tunnels, for example, bombs, mapping robots, and explosive gel. Many countries worry that civilians die in these attacks, and they ask Israel to plan them carefully. Difficult words: ground operation (something what takes place on the ground, not in the air or on water), purpose (the reason why something exists), civilian (related to ordinary people, not soldiers). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The problem is that these tunnels are often in places where people live, like schools and religious places. The soldiers used special things to destroy the tunnels, for example, robots. The world worries about people who live in Gaza. The United States tells Israel to be careful. Many people die in these attacks. Difficult words: network (a group or system of things which connect), hide (to be in a place where nobody can see or find you), destroy (to damage or attack something so that it is not possible to use it anymore). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tesla’s Cybertruck, initially anticipated to start at 40,000 dollars, is now priced at 60,990 dollars, 50% higher than Elon Musk’s 2019 estimate. The stainless steel truck inspired by a James Bond film features an unconventional design. Musk claims it surpasses traditional trucks in utility and speed. Despite the higher price, experts predict appeal to a wealthier, niche market. Cybertruck faces competition from Ford, Rivian, and GM in the pickup market. Tesla’s reputation for innovation relies on the Cybertruck’s success amid softer EV demand. Musk addressed production challenges; however, he expects significant cash flow in 12-18 months. The longest-range Cybertruck falls short of 2019 promises. Musk targets a production rate of 250,000 units annually by 2025. Difficult words: unconventional (unusual), utility (the state of being useful or profitable), niche (a specialized segment of the market). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Musk says that the truck offers more utility and speed than usual trucks. Although the price is higher, experts believe it will attract rich people who want to have something special. Musk said that there were problems with production, but he expects higher cash flow in 12-18 months. Difficult words: unique (different from the others), utility (when something is useful or it brings money to someone), cash flow (the money which moves into and out of a company). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
